title: Compound nouns
subtitle: ice hockey, cashpoint, travel agent
summary: Put two words together to make a new noun, and learn everyday compounds such as cashpoint, income tax and traffic lights.

lesson.heading: How compound nouns are formed
lesson.text: We make a **compound noun** by putting two words (sometimes three) together to create a new idea. Compound nouns are very common in English.

examples.text: **Ice hockey** is a game of hockey played on ice.
**Public transport** is transport that can be used by the public.
A **campsite** is a place used for camping.
A **babysitter** is someone who looks after young children when their parents go out.
A **haircut** is the act of cutting someone's hair.

lesson.heading: More compounds and their meanings
rows: money you pay to the government out of your income
the first language you learn as a child
someone whose job is to make travel arrangements for you
someone who makes films for the cinema or television
the punctuation mark at the end of a sentence
a card you use to pay for things
a card with your name and photograph, to prove who you are
lesson.note: Your income is the total amount of money you receive every year from your work and other places.

lesson.heading: Everyday objects and people
rows: a machine in a wall where you get money
the red, amber and green lights that control cars
a place where two roads cross each other
a person who cuts and styles hair
a machine that dries your hair
the substance you use to clean your teeth
the small brush you clean your teeth with
a piece of furniture for keeping clothes in
a chair with wheels, for someone who cannot walk
dark glasses you wear in bright sun
jewellery you wear in your ears
someone who plays music on the radio or at discos

lesson.heading: One word or two?
lesson.text: Some compound nouns are written as one word, some have a hyphen, and many are written as two separate words. There is no easy rule, so check in a dictionary when you are not sure.

lesson.heading: Families of compounds
lesson.note: One part of a compound often gives you a whole group of new words.

lesson.text: The main stress is usually on the first part: 'haircut, 'income tax. But a few put it on the second part: public 'transport, full 'stop.

exercises.prompt: I got some money from the ___ on the corner of the street.
exercises.explanation: A cashpoint is a machine that gives you money from your bank account.

exercises.prompt: I booked our holiday through a ___ in the town centre.
exercises.explanation: A travel agent makes travel arrangements for you.

exercises.prompt: Match each compound noun with its definition.

pairs.right: what you use to clean your teeth
someone who plays music at discos
the mark at the end of a sentence

exercises.prompt: Put each compound noun in the right group.
We stayed on a very nice ___, but unfortunately our tent wasn't really big enough.
exercises.explanation: A campsite is a site used for camping.

exercises.prompt: He can't walk at all now, so he has to use a ___ to move around.
exercises.explanation: A wheelchair is a chair with wheels for someone who cannot walk.

exercises.prompt: Which compound noun means 'a card with your name, photograph and information to prove who you are'?
exercises.explanation: ID card is short for identity card.

exercises.prompt: Liz and Mark wanted to go out, but they couldn't find a ___ for the children.
exercises.explanation: A babysitter looks after young children when their parents go out.

exercises.prompt: When I'm driving I always wear ___ if it's very bright and sunny.
Most people have to pay ___ on their salary; the more you earn, the more you pay.
exercises.explanation: Income tax is the money you pay to the government out of your income.

exercises.prompt: Which compound noun means 'a game played on ice using sticks'?
exercises.explanation: Ice hockey is hockey played on ice.

exercises.statement: A birthday card, a bus stop and an income tax bill are all written as two separate words.
exercises.explanation: Correct. Many compound nouns are written as two words; others are one word, like wheelchair.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order to explain what a mother tongue is.
exercises.answer: Your mother tongue is the first language you learn as a child.
exercises.explanation: Mother tongue is a compound noun written as two words.
